comments.content: The `finalized` branch wraps the execution timestamp (which is in seconds) with `Timestamp::from_nanos`, but the non-finalized branch wraps the header timestamp (also in seconds) with `Timestamp::from_nanos` after a `try_into()` to u64. Both branches are treating seconds as nanoseconds. The finalized branch should use `Timestamp::from_secs(...)` and the non-finalized branch should drop the `try_into()` and use `Timestamp::from_secs(...)` directly. As written, the returned timestamps will be ~1e9x too small (interpreted as nanoseconds), which will break `WaitForTimestamp` comparisons.

`timestamp` here is in seconds (from the movement RPC), but it's being wrapped with `Timestamp::from_nanos`. This should be `Timestamp::from_secs(timestamp)`. Same issue in `voyager/modules/state/movement/src/main.rs`.
`timestamp` is in seconds but wrapped with `Timestamp::from_nanos`. Should be `Timestamp::from_secs(timestamp)`.

`Timestamp::from_nanos(...).try_into()` is a no-op conversion (Timestamp -> Timestamp). The `try_into().expect(...)` is dead code and can be removed. Same pattern in `voyager/modules/consensus/tendermint/src/main.rs`.
`Timestamp::from_nanos(...).try_into()` is a no-op conversion (Timestamp -> Timestamp). The `try_into().expect(...)` is dead code and can be removed.

`Timestamp::from_secs` will silently overflow for large `secs` values (u64 multiplication). Consider using `checked_mul` or documenting the precondition. Also, `Timestamp` is serialized as a bare u64 via derive; if the previous wire format was `i64` nanos, this is wire-compatible for positive values, but any negative timestamps (previously representable as i64) are no longer representable. Confirm no callers relied on negative timestamps.
